STATUS: answered

The points cover only NVIDIA, so no cross-company comparison is possible.

NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says it uses foundries such as TSMC and Samsung to produce its semiconductor wafers, so it names TSMC alongside a second foundry rather than as a sole source [0001045810-26-000021:0012]. It uses CoWoS technology for semiconductor packaging. It relies on subcontractors and contract manufacturers such as Hon Hai, Wistron and Fabrinet for assembly, testing and packaging, and buys memory from SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung [0001045810-26-000021:0012].

NVIDIA says it has expanded supplier relationships to build redundancy and resilience. Its supply chain is mainly concentrated in Asia, and it is expanding into the U.S. and Latin America [0001045810-26-000021:0012]. It may place non-cancellable inventory orders ahead of historical lead times, pay premiums, or provide deposits to secure supply and capacity [0001045810-26-000021:0012].

The excerpts name AMD and Intel as NVIDIA's competitors but give no information on AMD's or Intel's own foundry dependence or reliance on TSMC [0001045810-26-000021:0012].
